subject: Dedicated capacity: prompt mix and SLA sizing for ClearHealth
messages:
From: Nathan Reed <nathan@clearhealth.com>
To: kimberly.park@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 14 Feb 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated capacity ask: prompt mix + SLA targets

Hi Kimberly,

We're moving forward on a Dedicated capacity evaluation for ClearHealth and need a concise sizing exercise we can use for procurement. High level: our app is a clinical summarization and QA layer sitting on top of patient records. A few facts: 
- Typical session: user submits a short prompt plus some patient context; model returns a 150-400 token summary/answer.
- Expected peak concurrent users: 350 web sessions, but only ~20% active RPS during peak bursts (~70 concurrent requests).
- Prompt distribution: a lot of short follow-ups (~30 tokens) and some long chain prompts that include context windows (~200-600 tokens) for multi-doc summaries.

Could you send a short questionnaire or a sample template we can fill and a ballpark GPU count and sizing guidance (H100 vs A100 vs quantized instances)? Procurement wants the numbers to validate the monthly commit.

Attaching a small CSV with a week of anonymized request logs. Happy to hop on a quick call if easier.

Thanks,
Nathan
Product Ops, ClearHealth

Attachments: clearhealth_sample_logs.csv (CSV, 42KB)

From: kimberly.park@redwood.com
To: Nathan Reed <nathan@clearhealth.com>
Cc: dev.patel@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 14 Feb 2028 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask: prompt mix + SLA targets

Thanks Nathan — got the CSV and this is the right ask. I put Dev (pre-sales infra) and Marissa (commercial) on copy.

Two quick asks so we can produce an actionable sizing:
1) Can you confirm the average response length target (p50/p90) for the summarization endpoint? You listed 150–400 tokens; if p90 is closer to 600 that materially changes GPU throughput.
2) Do you require strict p95 inference latency targets (e.g., <300ms token latency or end-to-end <1s)?

I'll have Dev produce a lightweight worksheet with the prompt/response buckets and a recommended GPU mix (and options with quantization). Once we have those numbers we can return a 1-page footprint and a 30/60/90-day ramp plan for procurement.

Would you prefer the worksheet as a Google Sheet (we can share an editable copy) or a simple .xlsx?

—Kimberly Park
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: dev.patel@redwood.com
To: kimberly.park@redwood.com, Nathan Reed <nathan@clearhealth.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 15 Feb 2028 08:30:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Dedicated capacity ask: prompt mix + SLA targets

Nathan / Kimberly — I reviewed the sample logs. Below is a concise sizing worksheet and the assumptions that will drive the GPU count. I've kept it focused so procurement gets what they need to validate a commit.

Assumptions derived from CSV:
- Observed request mix (approx): short prompts (<50 tokens): 38%, medium (50–250 tokens): 42%, long (>250 tokens): 20%.
- Observed avg prompt tokens: 95 tokens; median response tokens: 240 tokens; p90 response: ~520 tokens (long tails).
- Peak concurrent requests observed in CSV (10 minute window): 68 concurrent active requests. We'll size to a safety factor of 1.5 for burst tolerance -> target concurrency = 102.

Simple throughput calc (for baseline):
- Avg tokens per request = prompt (95) + response (240) = 335 tokens.
- If we want to support 15 QPS sustained at peak (15 QPS * 335 tokens = 5,025 tokens/sec). With bursts to 30 QPS (15k tokens/sec).

Model/runtime assumptions:
- Using an LLM family equivalent to 13B-70B mix (Redwood-verified variants). Quantized int8 copies provide ~1.8–2.2x token/s improvement over FP16 under our runtime.
- On H100 (optimized kernels, continuous batching), rough sustained throughput per GPU for the customer's mix: 
  - FP16: ~12k–18k tokens/sec (depends on seq len and attention pattern)
  - int8 quant: ~20k–28k tokens/sec
- On A100, expect ~65–80% of H100 throughput for these workloads.

Recommendations (ballpark):
Option A — Cost-conscious (quantized)
- Target sustained peak: 30 QPS burst -> ~15k tokens/sec. Use int8 quant nodes.
- GPUs required (sustained safety factor): 2 H100s (quantized) provide ~40–56k tokens/sec headroom — comfortably handle bursts and leave room for increase.

Option B — Low-latency/strict SLA (FP16 preferred)
- To tighten tail latency and reduce batching, choose 4 A100 GPUs (FP16, smaller batch sizes) or 3 H100s if available. This reduces queueing and keeps p95 generation latency below targeted thresholds.

Operational knobs to reduce GPU count:
- Prefix/KV cache for common patient context blocks (estimated 18–30% token reduction for repeated context).
- Small-batch async streaming to keep p95 stable while amortizing kernel costs.
- Rate-based admission control for large long-context requests during bursts.

Deliverables I'll attach: a one-sheet Excel that walks through the math (per-bucket qps -> tokens/s -> GPUs), and two example config snippets (batching and cache settings) to test in staging.

If you confirm p90 target and whether quantized is acceptable for clinical usage we can lock the numbers.

—Dev Patel
Principal Pre-Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachments: clearhealth_sizing_worksheet.xlsx (see attached)

From: marissa.cole@redwood.com
To: kimberly.park@redwood.com, dev.patel@redwood.com
Cc: Nathan Reed <nathan@clearhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Feb 2028 11:02:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Dedicated capacity ask: prompt mix + SLA targets

Nathan — adding commercial context.

High-level commercial options tied to the technical recommendations:
- Option 1 (2 H100 quantized) — Monthly committed plan, 12-month term, includes standard SLA (99.5% uptime) and console retention 30 days: estimated list price $XX,XXX / month (final pricing is in the attached quote).
- Option 2 (3 H100 FP16 or 4 A100 FP16) — Higher cost, shorter tail latency, 12-month term or 36-month with discount.

We can provide a 60-day evaluation commit at a reduced rate if you'd like to validate the numbers in prod — finance can do a time-limited pilot commit that converts to a full reserved contract.

Next steps: if the team is comfortable with Dev's Option A we can prepare an MSA addendum and a 60-day pilot PO to collect usage and validate prefix-cache savings.

—Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference

Attachment: CLH-quote-v1.pdf

From: Clara Mendez <clara.m@clearhealth.com>
To: kimberly.park@redwood.com
Cc: Nathan Reed <nathan@clearhealth.com>
Date: Fri, 17 Feb 2028 13:21:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask: prompt mix + SLA targets

Kimberly / Dev / Marissa — thanks for the quick turnaround. A few clarifications from our side after an internal review of the CSV: 
- p50 response target: 220 tokens; p90: 510 tokens (so Dev's p90 estimate is aligned).
- For compliance reasons we prefer FP16 for the highest-sensitivity workflows and are open to quantized for lower-sensitivity endpoints (clinical summarization can start quantized if we white-list the flows).
- We can start with the 60-day pilot commit on Option 1 but want to include a simple SLA-backed remediation if p95 latency exceeds 1.2s more than 3 times in a 30-day window.

I've attached a short set of anonymized logs (same schema) and a sample privacy appendix our legal team will use. Please confirm next steps and the expected delivery date for the sizing worksheet so procurement can prepare the PO.

Thanks,
Clara
Ops, ClearHealth

Attachments: clearhealth_sample_logs_2.csv, CLH_privacy_appendix.pdf

I'll take point on the pilot contract revisions with legal. Flagging that procurement will likely ask for an expanded reporting cadence (weekly token-level cost breakdown) — ensure the console retention for token breakdown is set to 90 days for the pilot.
